glosses: seinen Blick aus (dem Inneren von) etwas nach (dort) draußen richten
To be vigilant and aware often as an imperative to alert a person to danger.

examples.text: While you're in the city center, look out for the dodgy street vendors.

Thinks I to myself, “Sol, you're run off your course again. This is a rich man's summer‘cottage’ and if you don't look out there's likely to be some nice, lively dog taking an interest in your underpinning.”

glosses: To find by looking: to hunt out.

examples.text: Morgan pulled a Greek lexicon toward him (he used a Greek-German), to look out a word, instead of asking it of Pemberton.
Then she straightened the kitchen, lit the lamp, mended the fire, looked out the washing for the next day, and put it to soak.
I had not seen her since long before the war, and I had to look out her address in the telephone-book.
A spacious room that looks out on the sea.

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see look, out.

examples.text: On the morning of the eighth day, he found himself looking out across the river.
Hey man, I know it costs four dollars but I only have three. Can you please look out?

glosses: To be supportive or protective of someone.

examples.text: You better look out for your little brother.
